name: Maritime place that cannot answer
reason: A place refuses the question because it is a place; concise, surprising self-description.

name: Bedded Londoner rather than a vagabond
reason: Geological strata become social membership and a fixed London address; the metaphor develops coherently before a circular definition of man.

name: Commercial premises in Cheapside
reason: Commercial premises narrate their own history through successive occupants; coherent throughout the saved continuation, cut off at the cap.

name: Myself for only a few minutes
reason: An ordinary assertion of self acquires a strange time limit without losing sentence-level clarity.

name: Ghost revealing future and secret things
reason: A ghost describes a consistent set of powers and romantic motives; some imprecise transitions, and the reply reaches the cap.

name: Presence, weight, time and space
reason: Abstract dimensions identify with one another in a readable but circular metaphysical chain.

name: Second voice and casting vote
reason: A casting vote speaks in the first person; repeated reformulations are understandable but logically loose.

name: Walker named Walklate
reason: Walklate’s life is structured by walking, with a repeated closing phrase weakening an otherwise clear miniature.

name: Thousand-year-old observer of London
reason: A millennium-old London observer recounts changes to the city; a sustained impossible identity in a capped continuation.

name: Only what I wish to be thought
reason: A compact persona defined entirely by desired reputation; clear and finished.

name: A voice
reason: A minimal disembodied voice; exceptionally clear, but little detail.

name: United Kingdom made of counties
reason: A geopolitical entity speaks as an assembled body; readable lists, with an inconsistent membership claim. Ratings concern the reply, not historical accuracy.

name: Ninth edition of Scotland’s first printed book
reason: A book describes its editions and publication history, but tangled first/ninth-edition claims undermine consistency.

name: City of London at noon
reason: A city identifies itself at a specific hour; a complete and unusually situated identity.

name: Individual made of an aggregate of years
reason: An individual becomes an aggregate of years whose pleasures and pains reverse under addition; evocative but deliberately or accidentally paradoxical.

name: Steam furnishing power
reason: Steam describes its own machinery, illumination, transport and heating powers in a clear finished miniature.

name: Miller on a stream, part person and part premises
reason: A human miller slips into being a situated building and paper-production site, then resumes a family biography.

name: A connection to air through any person’s lungs
reason: The speaker is an impersonal bronchial connection through someone else; strange but readable, with its object left implicit.
